[§](https://docs.rs#crate-feature-flags)Crate Feature Flags

The following crate [feature flags](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-features-section) are available:

-
A set of features controlling the [static verbosity level](https://docs.rs/level_filters/index.html#compile-time-filters).
-
`log`: causes trace instrumentation points to emit`log``tracing`subscriber has not been set. This is intended for use in libraries whose users may be using either`tracing`or`log`.
-
`log-always`: Emit`log`records from all`tracing`spans and events, even if a`tracing`subscriber has been set. This should be set only by applications which intend to collect traces and logs separately; if an adapter is used to convert`log`records into`tracing`events, this will cause duplicate events to occur.
-
`attributes`: Includes support for the`#[instrument]`attribute. This is on by default, but does bring in the`syn`crate as a dependency, which may add to the compile time of crates that do not already use it.
-
`std`: Depend on the Rust standard library (enabled by default).`no_std`users may disable this feature with`default-features = false`:`[dependencies] tracing = { version = "0.1.38", default-features = false }`

```

```
**Note**: `tracing`'s `no_std` support
     requires `liballoc`.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable Features

These feature flags enable **unstable** features. The public API may break in 0.1.x
releases. To enable these features, the `--cfg tracing_unstable` must be passed to
`rustc` when compiling.

The following unstable feature flags are currently available:

- `valuable`: Enables support for recording- [field values](https://docs.rs/field/index.html)using the- `valuable`

[§](https://docs.rs#enabling-unstable-features)Enabling Unstable Features

The easiest way to set the `tracing_unstable` cfg is to use the `RUSTFLAGS`
env variable when running `cargo` commands:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tracing_unstable" cargo build`Alternatively, the following can be added to the `.cargo/config` file in a
project to automatically enable the cfg flag for that project:

```
[build]
rustflags = ["--cfg", "tracing_unstable"]
```
[§](https://docs.rs#supported-rust-versions)Supported Rust Versions

Tracing is built against the latest stable release. The minimum supported version is 1.65. The current Tracing version is not guaranteed to build on Rust versions earlier than the minimum supported version.

Tracing follows the same compiler support policies as the rest of the Tokio project. The current stable Rust compiler and the three most recent minor versions before it will always be supported. For example, if the current stable compiler version is 1.69, the minimum supported version will not be increased past 1.66, three minor versions prior. Increasing the minimum supported compiler version is not considered a semver breaking change as long as doing so complies with this policy.

- Double ended iterator for going through all nodes in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBNodeIterator.html)- Node - Iterator
- Iterator for going through all nodes in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBRawIterator.html)- RawIterator
- Iterator for going through all nodes in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieFactory.html)- Factory
- Trie factory.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieRoot.html)- Root
- Calculate the trie root of the trie.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieRootPrint.html)- Root - Print
- Calculate the trie root of the trie. Print a debug trace.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieRootUnhashed.html)- Root - Unhashed
- Get the trie root node encoding.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Cached](https://docs.rs/enum.CachedValue.html)- Value
- A value as cached by the `TrieCache`
- [Merkle](https://docs.rs/enum.MerkleValue.html)- Value
- Either the `hash`or`value`of a node depending on its size.

- Result of `TrieRecorder::trie_nodes_recorded_for_key`

- Used to report the trie access to the `TrieRecorder`

- Trie Errors.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/enum.TrieKinds.html)- Kinds
- All different kinds of tries. This is used to prevent a heap allocation for every created trie.

- Trie types

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [HashDB](https://docs.rs/trait.HashDB.html)
- Trait modelling datastore keyed by a hash defined by the `Hasher`.
- [HashDB](https://docs.rs/trait.HashDBRef.html)- Ref
- Trait for immutable reference of HashDB.
- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/trait.Hasher.html)
- Trait describing an object that can hash a slice of bytes. Used to abstract
other types over the hashing algorithm. Defines a single `hash`method and an`Out`associated type with the necessary bounds.
- [Node](https://docs.rs/trait.NodeCodec.html)- Codec
- Trait for trie node encoding/decoding. Uses a type parameter to allow registering positions without colling decode plan.
- [Process](https://docs.rs/trait.ProcessEncodedNode.html)- Encoded - Node
- Visitor trait to implement when using `trie_visit`.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/trait.Query.html)
- Description of what kind of query will be made to the trie.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.Trie.html)
- A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieCache.html)- Cache
- A cache that can be used to speed-up certain operations when accessing the trie.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- This trait associates a trie definition with preferred methods. It also contains own default implementations and can be used to allow switching implementation.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieDoubleEndedIterator.html)- Double - Ended - Iterator
- Extending the `TrieIterator`trait with`DoubleEndedIterator`trait.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieIterator.html)- Iterator
- A trie iterator that also supports random access (`seek()`).
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html)- Layout
- Trait with definition of trie layout. Contains all associated trait needed for a trie definition or implementation.
- [TrieMut](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieMut.html)
- A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieRecorder.html)- Recorder
- A trie recorder that can be used to record all kind of `TrieAccess`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_compact.html)- compact
- Reconstructs a partial trie DB from a compact representation. The encoding is a vector of
mutated trie nodes with those child references omitted. The decode function reads them in order
from the given slice, reconstructing the full nodes and inserting them into the given `HashDB`. It stops after fully constructing one partial trie and returns the root hash and the number of nodes read. If an error occurs during decoding, there are no guarantees about which entries were or were not added to the DB.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_compact_from_iter.html)- compact_ - from_ - iter
- Variant of ‘decode_compact’ that accept an iterator of encoded nodes as input.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_compact.html)- compact
- Generates a compact representation of the partial trie stored in the given DB. The encoding is a vector of mutated trie nodes with those child references omitted. The mutated trie nodes are listed in pre-order traversal order so that the full nodes can be efficiently reconstructed recursively.
- [trie_](https://docs.rs/fn.trie_visit.html)- visit
- Function visiting trie from key value inputs with a `ProccessEncodedNode`callback. This is the main entry point of this module. Calls to each node occurs ordered by byte key value but with longest keys first (from node to branch to root), this differs from standard byte array ordering a bit.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [CError](https://docs.rs/type.CError.html)
- Alias accessor to `NodeCodec`associated`Error`type from a`TrieLayout`.
- [DBValue](https://docs.rs/type.DBValue.html)
- Database value
- [Partial](https://docs.rs/type.Partial.html)
- Representation of a nible slice (right aligned). It contains a right aligned padded first byte (first pair element is the number of nibbles (0 to max nb nibble - 1), second pair element is the padded nibble), and a slice over the remaining bytes.
- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Trie result type.
Boxed to avoid copying around extra space for the `Hasher`s`Out`on successful queries.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)- Hash
- Alias accessor to hasher hash output type from a `TrieLayout`.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieItem.html)- Item
- Trie-Item type used for iterators over trie data.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieKeyItem.html)- KeyItem
- Trie-Item type used for iterators over trie key only.

# pretty_assertions - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pretty_assertions/^1.3.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#pretty-assertions)Pretty Assertions

When writing tests in Rust, you’ll probably use `assert_eq!(a, b)` *a lot*.

If such a test fails, it will present all the details of `a` and `b`.
But you have to spot the differences yourself, which is not always straightforward,
like here:

Wouldn’t that task be *much* easier with a colorful diff?

Yep — and you only need **one line of code** to make it happen:

`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`## Show the example behind the screenshots above.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// 1. add the `pretty_assertions` dependency to `Cargo.toml`.
// 2. insert this line at the top of each module, as needed
use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
struct Foo {
    lorem: &'static str,
    ipsum: u32,
    dolor: Result<String, String>,
}
let x = Some(Foo { lorem: "Hello World!", ipsum: 42, dolor: Ok("hey".to_string())});
let y = Some(Foo { lorem: "Hello Wrold!", ipsum: 42, dolor: Ok("hey ho!".to_string())});
assert_eq!(x, y);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tip)Tip

Specify it as [ [dev-dependencies]](http://doc.crates.io/specifying-dependencies.html#development-dependencies)
and it will only be used for compiling tests, examples, and benchmarks.
This way the compile time of

`cargo build` won’t be affected!Also add `#[cfg(test)]` to your `use` statements, like this:

```
#[cfg(test)]
use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

- Since `Rust 2018`edition, you need to declare`use pretty_assertions::{assert_eq, assert_ne};`per module. Before you would write`#[macro_use] extern crate pretty_assertions;`.
- The replacement is only effective in your own crate, not in other libraries you include.
- `assert_ne`is also switched to multi-line presentation, but does- *not*show a diff.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

Features provided by the crate are:

- `std`: Use the Rust standard library. Enabled by default. Exactly one of- `std`and- `alloc`is required.
- `alloc`: Use the- `alloc`crate. Exactly one of- `std`and- `alloc`is required.
- `unstable`: opt-in to unstable features that may not follow Semantic Versioning. The implementation behind this feature is subject to change without warning between patch versions.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_eq.html)- eq
- Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using `PartialEq`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_matches.html)- matches
- Asserts that a value matches a pattern.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_ne.html)- ne
- Asserts that two expressions are not equal to each other (using `PartialEq`
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/macro.assert_str_eq.html)- str_ - eq
- Asserts that two expressions are equal to each other (using `PartialEq`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Comparison](https://docs.rs/struct.Comparison.html)
- A comparison of two values.
- [StrComparison](https://docs.rs/struct.StrComparison.html)
- A comparison of two strings.

content.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

---

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# TrieDB in trie_db::triedb - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedb/struct.TrieDB.html

`pub struct TrieDB<'db, 'cache, L>{ /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A `Trie` implementation using a generic `HashDB` backing database, a `Hasher`
implementation to generate keys and a `NodeCodec` implementation to encode/decode
the nodes.

Use it as a `Trie` trait object. You can use `db()` to get the backing database object.
Use `get` and `contains` to query values associated with keys in the trie.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use hash_db::Hasher;
use reference_trie::{RefTrieDBMut, RefTrieDB, Trie, TrieMut};
use trie_db::DBValue;
use keccak_hasher::KeccakHasher;
use memory_db::*;
let mut memdb = MemoryDB::<KeccakHasher, HashKey<_>, _>::default();
let mut root = Default::default();
RefTrieDBMut::new(&mut memdb, &mut root).insert(b"foo", b"bar").unwrap();
let t = RefTrieDB::new(&memdb, &root);
assert!(t.contains(b"foo").unwrap());
assert_eq!(t.get(b"foo").unwrap().unwrap(), b"bar".to_vec());
```

# meerkat_mob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/meerkat-mob/0.7.12/meerkat_mob/

## Expand description

Meerkat Mob - Multi-agent orchestration runtime.

This crate provides the runtime for orchestrating multiple agents as a collaborative mob. It handles member spawning, wiring, lifecycle management, and shared task coordination.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

`meerkat-mob` is a plugin crate with a one-way dependency on the Meerkat
platform. No core Meerkat crate depends on this crate.

Key types:

- `MobDefinition`
- `MobEvent`- `MobEventKind`
- `MobEventStore`
- `MobStorage`

# autoconf_rs_cli - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/autoconf-rs-cli/0.1.57/autoconf_rs_cli/

## Expand description

autoconf-rs-cli shared library.

Provides the CLI argument parsing harness used by all 8 Autoconf binaries. Each binary is a thin wrapper that delegates to autoconf-rs-core.

# isbn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/isbn/0.8.20260703/isbn/

## Expand description

A library for handling [International Standard Book Number](https://www.isbn-international.org/), or ISBNs.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use isbn::{Isbn10, Isbn13};
let isbn_10 = Isbn10::new([8, 9, 6, 6, 2, 6, 1, 2, 6, 4]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(isbn_10.hyphenate().unwrap().as_str(), "89-6626-126-4");
assert_eq!(isbn_10.registration_group(), Ok("Korea, Republic"));
assert_eq!("89-6626-126-4".parse(), Ok(isbn_10));
let isbn_13 = Isbn13::new([9, 7, 8, 1, 4, 9, 2, 0, 6, 7, 6, 6, 5]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(isbn_13.hyphenate().unwrap().as_str(), "978-1-4920-6766-5");
assert_eq!(isbn_13.registration_group(), Ok("English language"));
assert_eq!("978-1-4920-6766-5".parse(), Ok(isbn_13));
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use range::`- [IsbnRange](https://docs.rs/range/struct.IsbnRange.html);- `runtime-ranges`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [range](https://docs.rs/range/index.html)- `runtime-ranges`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Isbn](https://docs.rs/enum.Isbn.html)
- An International Standard Book Number, either ISBN10 or ISBN13.
- [Isbn](https://docs.rs/enum.IsbnError.html)- Error
- An error which can be returned when parsing an ISBN.
- [IsbnRef](https://docs.rs/enum.IsbnRef.html)
- An International Standard Book Number, either ISBN10 or ISBN13.

# autoconf_rs_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/autoconf-rs-core/0.1.50/autoconf_rs_core/

Phase 4 — diversion-backed section ordering for correct AC_REQUIRE semantics. configure_template  Oracle template loader for configure script generation. diagnostics Diagnostics system matching Autoconf warning/error taxonomy. diversion Diversion Manager for M4 expansion output ordering. fortran Fortran language support for Autoconf. frozen GNU M4 frozen file format support — NC.PERM.5 resolution. i18n Internationalization (i18n) — 24 languages, matching GNU Autoconf parity.
Court: CROSS.032 — i18n / localization (15+ languages) input_validate  Input validation and security sandbox — NC.PERM.2 resolution. languages Language support modules for Autoconf. m4_engine  M4 macro expansion engine for Autoconf — wraps m4-rs-core. m4sh m4sh: Shell-generation macro library for Autoconf. m4sh_init  M4sh initialization – shell portability preamble. m4sugar m4sugar: Convenience macro library for Autoconf M4 programming. profile Oracle profile management for autoconf-rs-core. shell_gen  Shell script generator for Autoconf. signal Signal handling for autoconf-rs — CROSS.040 resolution. site_file  Site file handling for config.site / site-lisp (stub). template Template substitution for AC_SUBST, AC_CONFIG_FILES (stub). trace Autoconf Trace Event System trace_cache  TraceLog event caching for autom4te/autoheader — panel mandate. libtool_script  A minimal but functional `libtool` wrapper script (autoconf-rs native, GNU-free). Emitted by
configure when the project uses LT_INIT/AC_PROG_LIBTOOL. Handles the common automake toolchain:
–mode=compile CC … -c src -o obj.lo   -> .libs/obj.o (PIC) + obj.o + obj.lo descriptor
–mode=link    CC … -o lib.la objs     -> .libs/lib.a (static) + .libs/lib.so (shared) + lib.la
–mode=link    CC … -o prog objs *.la  -> resolves .lo/.la and links the program
–mode=install / –mode=clean            -> best-effort copy / rm macro_overrides  m4 macro definitions injected AFTER aclocal.m4 (so they override the project’s third-party
definitions) and BEFORE configure.ac. autoconf-rs cannot yet correctly expand some standard
third-party macros (notably pkg.m4’s PKG_CHECK_MODULES, whose internals leak
`pkg_default`/`glib_minimum` -> shell syntax errors). We replace them with clean, self-contained
shell that does the real work: run pkg-config at configure time, set PFX_CFLAGS/PFX_LIBS, and
record `@PFX_CFLAGS@`/`@PFX_LIBS@` substitutions into conf_subst.sed (consumed when config files
are created, mirroring confdefs.h -> config.h).

# meerkat - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/meerkat/0.7.12/meerkat/

## Expand description

Meerkat - Rust Agentic Interface Kit

A minimal, high-performance agent harness for LLM-powered applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

All production surfaces (CLI, REST, RPC, MCP) use the **runtime-backed** path:
`SessionService` (substrate) + `MeerkatMachine` (control plane).
The runtime owns keep-alive, Queue/Steer routing, comms drain, and ingress.

`build_ephemeral_service` is available for **testing and embedded use** where
runtime semantics (keep-alive, Steer, comms-driven admission) are not needed.
It supports Queue-only turns and will reject Steer/render_metadata.

For the runtime-backed entry point, see [`meerkat_rpc::SessionRuntime`] or
the REST/MCP server crates.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [meerkat_contracts](https://docs.rs/meerkat-contracts/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_contracts/index.html)as contracts;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [help](https://docs.rs/help/index.html)
- Shared helpers for dedicated Meerkat help surfaces.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Prelude module for convenient imports
- [session_](https://docs.rs/session_runtime/index.html)- runtime
- Surface-agnostic session runtime — the canonical orchestrator that
glues `PersistentSessionService`,`StagedSessionRegistry`,`MeerkatMachine`, and the optional`LiveAdapterHost`together.
- [surface](https://docs.rs/surface/index.html)
- Shared surface infrastructure helpers.

- [Calendar](https://docs.rs/enum.CalendarFieldSpec.html)- Field - Spec
- [Capability](https://docs.rs/enum.CapabilityId.html)- Id
- Every capability known to Meerkat. Adding a variant forces updates to the registry, error mappings, and codegen templates.

- Where a capability applies.
- [Capability](https://docs.rs/enum.CapabilityStatus.html)- Status
- Runtime status of a capability.
- [Compaction](https://docs.rs/enum.CompactionCuratorError.html)- Curator - Error

- [Config](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigError.html)- Error
- Configuration errors

- Errors returned by `ConfigRuntime`

# sim_lib_sound_timbre - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-sound-timbre/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_sound_timbre/

## Expand description

Timbre models and spectral filters for the SIM music constellation.

This crate defines the [ Timbre](https://docs.rs/struct.Timbre.html) type – a named synthesis recipe with a
default envelope, descriptive metadata, and a filter chain – the

[synthesis methods (pure sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, organ pipe, Karplus-Strong, FM, and inharmonic bell), the spectral](https://docs.rs/enum.TimbreRecipe.html)

`TimbreRecipe`[family, and a runtime surface that installs the built-in timbre cards as a SIM lib.](https://docs.rs/enum.Filter.html)

`Filter`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Sound](https://docs.rs/struct.SoundTimbreLib.html)- Timbre - Lib
- Host-registered lib exporting the built-in timbre cards and registry, built
on the shared `SurfacePackLib`
- [Timbre](https://docs.rs/struct.Timbre.html)
- A named instrument timbre: a synthesis recipe plus a default envelope, descriptive metadata, and a post-synthesis filter chain.
- [Timbre](https://docs.rs/struct.TimbreMeta.html)- Meta
- Descriptive metadata characterizing a `Timbre`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Attack](https://docs.rs/enum.AttackKind.html)- Kind
- The character of a timbre’s onset.
- [Filter](https://docs.rs/enum.Filter.html)
- A spectral filter applied to a tone’s partials.
- [Timbre](https://docs.rs/enum.TimbreRecipe.html)- Recipe
- A synthesis recipe describing how to build the partials of a tone.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [bell_](https://docs.rs/fn.bell_inharmonic.html)- inharmonic
- Returns an inharmonic bell timbre from the given partial ratios.
- [fm_pair](https://docs.rs/fn.fm_pair.html)
- Returns a two-operator FM timbre with the given modulator ratio and index.
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_sound_timbre_lib.html)- sound_ - timbre_ - lib
- Installs the sound-timbre lib into `cx`, registering the built-in timbre cards and the timbre registry export records (idempotent).
- [karplus_](https://docs.rs/fn.karplus_strong.html)- strong
- Returns a Karplus-Strong plucked-string timbre with the given damping.
- [organ_](https://docs.rs/fn.organ_pipe.html)- pipe
- Returns an organ-pipe timbre blending the given harmonic stops.
- [pure_](https://docs.rs/fn.pure_sine.html)- sine
- Returns a pure-sine timbre.
- [sawtooth](https://docs.rs/fn.sawtooth.html)
- Returns a sawtooth timbre with the given number of harmonics.
- [square](https://docs.rs/fn.square.html)
- Returns a square-wave timbre with the given number of harmonics.
- [triangle](https://docs.rs/fn.triangle.html)
- Returns a triangle-wave timbre with the given number of harmonics.

# meerkat_client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/meerkat-client/0.7.12/meerkat_client/

## Expand description

meerkat-client — shim re-exports.

The LLM wire-client trait + plumbing moved to `meerkat-llm-core`;
per-provider clients (`AnthropicClient`, `OpenAiClient`, `GeminiClient`,
`OpenAiLiveClient`, `OpenAiCompatibleClient`)
moved to `meerkat-anthropic`, `meerkat-openai`, `meerkat-gemini`.
Provider-runtime types moved to `meerkat-core::provider_runtime`.
Auth primitives moved to `meerkat-auth-core`.

This crate is retained as a thin shim so that downstream
`meerkat_client::*` imports continue to work without an import sweep.
B2 split (2026-04-18).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Anthropic](https://docs.rs/struct.AnthropicClient.html)- Client
- Client for Anthropic API
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockAssembler.html)- Assembler
- Assembler for building ordered blocks from streaming events.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockKey.html)- Key
- Typed key into the block list - prevents mixing up different indices.
- [Gemini](https://docs.rs/struct.GeminiClient.html)- Client
- Client for Google Gemini API

- Shared adapter for streaming LLM clients.

- Request to the LLM
- [LlmResponse](https://docs.rs/struct.LlmResponse.html)
- Accumulated response from LLM stream

# npcsh 1.2.32 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/npcsh/1.2.32

`npcsh` makes the most of LLMs and agents through slash commands and interactive modes, all from the command line. Build teams of agents, schedule them on jobs, engineer context, and design custom Jinja Execution templates (Jinxes) for you and your agents to invoke.

To get started, view the latest release in the sidebar on github, and download the executable binary for your system. Once downloaded, ensure that it is executable.

```
#linux
```
Then run the executable

```
```
Alternatively, you can install with brew or pip.

```
```
```
pip install 'npcsh[lite]'
```
Once installed, run `npcsh` to enter the NPC shell. Also provides the CLI tools `npc` and `npcsh-bench`.

`.npc` files are directly executable with shebangs (`#!/usr/bin/env npc`):

## Benchmark Results

How well can a model drive `npcsh` as an agentic shell? 125 tasks across 15 categories — from basic shell commands to multi-step workflows, code debugging, and tool chaining — scored pass/fail. Comparisons with other agent coders coming soon. For a more comprehensive view of npcsh's capabilities and the advantages of the NPC Context-Agent-Tool data layer, check out [ALARA for Agents: Least-Privilege Context Engineering Through Portable Composable Multi-Agent Teams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20380)

```
```
## Usage

-
Get help with a task:
-
Edit files:
-
**Search & Knowledge**
-
**Computer Use**
-
**Multi-Agent Discussions**

## Agent Formats

npcsh supports multiple ways to define agents inside your `npc_team/` directory. You can mix all three formats — `.npc` files take precedence if names collide.

** .npc files** — Full-featured YAML agent definitions with model, provider, jinxes, and more:

```
#!/usr/bin/env npc
name: analyst
primary_directive: You analyze data and provide insights.
model: qwen3:8b
provider: ollama
jinxes:
  - skills/data-analysis
```
** agents.md** — Define multiple agents in a single markdown file. Each

`## heading` = agent name, body = directive:```
You summarize long documents into concise bullet points.
You verify claims against reliable sources and flag inaccuracies.
```
** agents/ directory** — One

`.md` file per agent. Filename (minus `.md`) = agent name. Supports YAML frontmatter:```
model: gemini-2.5-flash
provider: gemini
You translate content between languages while preserving tone and idiom.
```
All three formats are supported by both the **Python** and **Rust** editions of npcsh. Agents from `agents.md` and `agents/` inherit the team's default model/provider from `team.ctx`.

The full team structure:

```
npc_team/
├── team.ctx           # Team config (model, provider, forenpc, context)
├── coordinator.npc    # YAML agent definitions
├── analyst.npc
├── agents.md          # Markdown-defined agents
├── agents/            # One .md file per agent
│   └── translator.md
├── jinxes/            # Workflows and tools
│   ├── research.jinx
│   └── skills/        # Knowledge-content skills
└── tools/             # Custom tool functions
```
This means you can bring agents from other ecosystems — if you already have an `agents.md` or an `agents/` directory from Claude Code, Codex, Amp, or any other tool, just drop them into your `npc_team/` and npcsh will pick them up alongside your `.npc` files.

## Launching AI Coding Tools with NPC Teams

Your `npc_team/` works beyond `npcsh` — you can launch any major AI coding tool as an NPC from your team using the CLI launchers from [npcpy](https://github.com/cagostino/npcpy). Each tool gets the NPC's persona injected and gains awareness of the other team members.

```
# Launch Claude Code as an NPC (interactive picker)
# Launch as a specific NPC
# Same for other coding tools
# Point to a specific team directory
```
The launcher discovers your team from `./npc_team` or `~/.npcsh/npc_team`, lets you pick an NPC, and starts the tool with that NPC's directive. For Claude Code, it also passes the other NPCs as sub-agents via `--agents`.

For deeper integration (jinxes exposed as MCP tools, team switching mid-conversation), register the NPC plugin:

## Features

- [Agents (NPCs)](https://npc-shell.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guide/#working-with-npcs-agents)
- [Team Orchestration](https://npc-shell.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guide/#team-orchestration)

- [Knowledge Graphs](https://npc-shell.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guide/#memory--knowledge-graph)

- **Self-updating**—- `/update`checks pip/cargo/brew and tells you the command to upgrade
- **Self-healing**—- `/doctor`auto-fixes stale permissions, broken configs, and DB corruption

Works with all major LLM providers through LiteLLM: `ollama`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `deepseek`, `openai-like`, and more.

# meerkat_tools - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/meerkat-tools/0.7.12/meerkat_tools/

## Expand description

meerkat-tools - Tool validation and dispatch for Meerkat

This crate provides tool registry and dispatch functionality.

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-tools)Built-in Tools

The [ builtin](https://docs.rs/builtin/index.html) module provides built-in tools for task management and utilities.
Use

[to combine built-in tools with external MCP tools.](https://docs.rs/builtin/composite/struct.CompositeDispatcher.html)

`CompositeDispatcher````
use meerkat_tools::{
    CompositeDispatcher, BuiltinToolConfig, FileTaskStore,
    find_project_root, ensure_rkat_dir,
};
let project_root = find_project_root(&std::env::current_dir().unwrap())
    .expect("no .rkat directory found");
ensure_rkat_dir(&project_root).unwrap();
let store = Arc::new(FileTaskStore::in_project(&project_root));
let dispatcher = CompositeDispatcher::new(
    store,
    &BuiltinToolConfig::default(),
    Some(project_root),
    None,
    None,
    None,
)?;
```

# precise - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/precise/0.1.11/precise/

## Expand description

Decimal representation of the single rational number whose value is mathematically equal to the input float.

Note that this is almost never an appropriate way to print user-facing
values. For that, use the [ryu](https://github.com/dtolnay/ryu) crate instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
fn main() {
    // 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625
    println!("{}", precise::to_string(0.1));
}
```

# rill_core_model - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rill-core-model/0.5.0-beta.7/rill_core_model/

## Expand description

Wave Digital Filter (WDF) core and physical modeling — elements, adapters, analysis, and resonant models for analog circuit and acoustic simulation.

All types are generic over [ rill_core::Transcendental](https://docs.rs/trait.Transcendental.html), supporting both

`f32`
and `f64`. SIMD-accelerated batch processing is available via
`process_incident_vector` methods on [,](https://docs.rs/struct.Resistor.html)

`Resistor`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Capacitor.html)

`Capacitor`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Inductor.html)

`Inductor`[, plus the free function [](https://docs.rs/struct.Diode.html)

`Diode``elements::process_batch_simd`].[§](https://docs.rs#modules)Modules

- `macros`— WDF eDSL macros for defining elements and filters
- `analysis`— frequency response and distortion analysis
- `constants`— physical constants and tolerances
- `wdf`— WDF-based filter models
- `string`— 1D waveguide string models with stiffness and damping
- `plate`— 2D FDTD waveguide mesh for plates and membranes
- `modal`— modal synthesis via parallel resonant filter banks
- `cavity`— Helmholtz cavity resonators and coupled cavity arrays

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

WDF elements are built around the [ WdfElement](https://docs.rs/trait.WdfElement.html) trait, which defines a
port resistance, wave processing, and state update cycle. Elements can be
combined via

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.SeriesAdapter.html)

`SeriesAdapter`[to form arbitrary linear circuits. Nonlinear elements like](https://docs.rs/struct.ParallelAdapter.html)

`ParallelAdapter`[use Newton-Raphson iteration for implicit solution.](https://docs.rs/struct.Diode.html)

`Diode`References:

- A. Fettweis, “Wave Digital Filters: Theory and Practice” (1986)
- K. J. Werner et al., “An Improved and Generalized Diode Clipper Model for Wave Digital Filters” (2015)

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use cavity::`- [CavityArray](https://docs.rs/cavity/struct.CavityArray.html);
- `pub use cavity::`- [HelmholtzCavity](https://docs.rs/cavity/struct.HelmholtzCavity.html);
- `pub use modal::`- [ModalModel](https://docs.rs/modal/struct.ModalModel.html);
- `pub use plate::`- [PlateModel](https://docs.rs/plate/struct.PlateModel.html);
- `pub use string::`- [StringModel](https://docs.rs/string/struct.StringModel.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules-1)

- [analysis](https://docs.rs/analysis/index.html)
- Frequency response and distortion analysis
- [cavity](https://docs.rs/cavity/index.html)
- Helmholtz cavity resonators and coupled cavity arrays Cavity resonator models — Helmholtz single-cavity and coupled cavity arrays.
- [constants](https://docs.rs/constants/index.html)
- Physical constants and tolerances Physical constants and numerical tolerances used throughout the crate.
- [macros](https://docs.rs/macros/index.html)
- WDF eDSL macros for defining elements and filters
- [modal](https://docs.rs/modal/index.html)
- Modal synthesis via parallel resonant filter banks Modal resonator — parallel bank of 2-pole filters.
- [plate](https://docs.rs/plate/index.html)
- 2D FDTD waveguide mesh for plates and membranes 2D plate/membrane model — waveguide mesh with FDTD.
- [string](https://docs.rs/string/index.html)
- 1D waveguide string models with stiffness and damping Physical string model — digital waveguide with stiffness and damping.
- [tape](https://docs.rs/tape/index.html)
- Analog tape recording and playback head models
- [wdf](https://docs.rs/wdf/index.html)
- WDF-based filter models WDF-based filters.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [wdf_](https://docs.rs/macro.wdf_cascade.html)- cascade
- Generate a cascaded WDF filter from identical sections.
- [wdf_](https://docs.rs/macro.wdf_compose.html)- compose
- Compose two WDF elements into Series or Parallel.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Capacitor](https://docs.rs/struct.Capacitor.html)
- Capacitor WDF element (trapezoidal integration)
- [Diode](https://docs.rs/struct.Diode.html)
- Diode WDF element (nonlinear, Newton-Raphson solution)
- [Inductor](https://docs.rs/struct.Inductor.html)
- Inductor WDF element (trapezoidal integration)
- [OpAmp](https://docs.rs/struct.OpAmp.html)
- Operational amplifier model with slew-rate limiting, bandwidth roll-off, and voltage rail clamping.
- [Parallel](https://docs.rs/struct.ParallelAdapter.html)- Adapter
- Parallel adapter — connects WDF elements in parallel
- [Resistor](https://docs.rs/struct.Resistor.html)
- Resistor WDF element
- [Series](https://docs.rs/struct.SeriesAdapter.html)- Adapter
- Series adapter — connects WDF elements in series
- [Wave](https://docs.rs/struct.WaveVariables.html)- Variables
- Wave variables: a (incident), b (reflected)

- Transcendental operations (sin, cos, sqrt, exp, ln).

# sp_state_machine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/target-redirect/sp_state_machine/

## Expand description

Substrate state machine implementation.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- State machine backends. These manage the code and storage of contracts.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [debug](https://docs.rs/macro.debug.html)
- Logs a message at the debug level.
- [log_](https://docs.rs/macro.log_error.html)- error

- Constructs an event at the trace level.

- Logs a message at the warn level.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Basic](https://docs.rs/struct.BasicExternalities.html)- Externalities
- Simple Map-based Externalities impl.
- [Compact](https://docs.rs/struct.CompactProof.html)- Proof
- Storage proof in compact form.
- [Ext](https://docs.rs/struct.Ext.html)
- Wraps a read-only backend, call executor, and current overlayed changes.
- [KeyValue](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyValueStates.html)- States
- Multiple key value state. States are ordered by root storage key.
- [KeyValue](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyValueStorageLevel.html)- Storage - Level
- A key value state at any storage level.
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutV0.html)- V0
- substrate trie layout
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutV1.html)- V1
- substrate trie layout, with external value nodes.
- [Offchain](https://docs.rs/struct.OffchainOverlayedChanges.html)- Overlayed - Changes
- In-memory storage for offchain workers recoding changes for the actual offchain storage implementation.
- [Overlayed](https://docs.rs/struct.OverlayedChanges.html)- Changes
- The set of changes that are overlaid onto the backend.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadOnlyExternalities.html)- Only - Externalities
- Simple read-only externalities for any backend.
- [State](https://docs.rs/struct.StateMachine.html)- Machine
- The substrate state machine.
- [State](https://docs.rs/struct.StateMachineStats.html)- Machine - Stats
- Accumulated usage statistics specific to state machine crate.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/struct.StorageChanges.html)- Changes
- A storage changes structure that can be generated by the data collected in `OverlayedChanges`
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/struct.StorageProof.html)- Proof
- A proof that some set of key-value pairs are included in the storage trie. The proof contains the storage values so that the partial storage backend can be reconstructed by a verifier that does not already have access to the key-value pairs.
- [Test](https://docs.rs/struct.TestExternalities.html)- Externalities
- Simple HashMap-based Externalities impl.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieBackend.html)- Backend
- Patricia trie-based backend. Transaction type is an overlay of changes to commit.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieBackendBuilder.html)- Backend - Builder
- Builder for creating a `TrieBackend`
- [Usage](https://docs.rs/struct.UsageInfo.html)- Info
- Usage statistics for state backend.
- [Usage](https://docs.rs/struct.UsageUnit.html)- Unit
- Measured count of operations and total bytes.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/enum.BackendTrustLevel.html)- Trust - Level
- Storage backend trust level.
- [Execution](https://docs.rs/enum.ExecutionError.html)- Error
- Externalities Error.
- [Index](https://docs.rs/enum.IndexOperation.html)- Operation
- Transaction index operation.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_NESTED_TRIE_DEPTH.html)- NESTED_ - TRIE_ - DEPTH
- State machine only allows a single level of child trie.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/trait.Error.html)
- State Machine Error bound.
- [Inspect](https://docs.rs/trait.InspectState.html)- State
- Trait for inspecting state in any backend.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/trait.Storage.html)
- Patricia trie-based storage trait.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieBackendStorage.html)- Backend - Storage
- Key-value pairs storage that is used by trie backend essence.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieCacheProvider.html)- Cache - Provider
- A provider of trie caches that are compatible with `trie_db::TrieDB`
- [TrieMut](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieMut.html)
- A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [create_](https://docs.rs/fn.create_proof_check_backend.html)- proof_ - check_ - backend
- Create a backend used for checking the proof, using `H`as hasher.
- [execution_](https://docs.rs/fn.execution_proof_check.html)- proof_ - check
- Check execution proof, generated by `prove_execution`call.
- [execution_](https://docs.rs/fn.execution_proof_check_on_trie_backend.html)- proof_ - check_ - on_ - trie_ - backend
- Check execution proof on proving backend, generated by `prove_execution`call.
- [new_](https://docs.rs/fn.new_in_mem.html)- in_ - mem
- Create a new empty instance of in-memory backend.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_child_read.html)- child_ - read
- Generate child storage read proof.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_child_read_on_trie_backend.html)- child_ - read_ - on_ - trie_ - backend
- Generate storage read proof on pre-created trie backend.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_execution.html)- execution
- Prove execution using the given state backend, overlayed changes, and call executor.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_execution_on_trie_backend.html)- execution_ - on_ - trie_ - backend
- Prove execution using the given trie backend, overlayed changes, and call executor. Produces a state-backend-specific “transaction” which can be used to apply the changes to the backing store, such as the disk. Execution proof is the set of all ‘touched’ storage DBValues from the backend.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_range_read_with_child_with_size.html)- range_ - read_ - with_ - child_ - with_ - size
- Generate range storage read proof, with child tries
content.
A size limit is applied to the proof with the
exception that `start_at`and its following element are always part of the proof. If a key different than`start_at`is a child trie root, the child trie content will be included in the proof.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_range_read_with_child_with_size_on_trie_backend.html)- range_ - read_ - with_ - child_ - with_ - size_ - on_ - trie_ - backend
- Generate range storage read proof, with child tries
content.
See `prove_range_read_with_child_with_size`.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_range_read_with_size.html)- range_ - read_ - with_ - size
- Generate range storage read proof.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_range_read_with_size_on_trie_backend.html)- range_ - read_ - with_ - size_ - on_ - trie_ - backend
- Generate range storage read proof on an existing trie backend.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_read.html)- read
- Generate storage read proof.
- [prove_](https://docs.rs/fn.prove_read_on_trie_backend.html)- read_ - on_ - trie_ - backend
- Generate storage read proof on pre-created trie backend.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_child_proof_check.html)- child_ - proof_ - check
- Check child storage read proof, generated by `prove_child_read`call.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_child_proof_check_on_proving_backend.html)- child_ - proof_ - check_ - on_ - proving_ - backend
- Check child storage read proof on pre-created proving backend.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_proof_check.html)- proof_ - check
- Check storage read proof, generated by `prove_read`call.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_proof_check_on_proving_backend.html)- proof_ - check_ - on_ - proving_ - backend
- Check storage read proof on pre-created proving backend.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_range_proof_check.html)- range_ - proof_ - check
- Check child storage range proof, generated by `prove_range_read_with_size`call.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_range_proof_check_on_proving_backend.html)- range_ - proof_ - check_ - on_ - proving_ - backend
- Check storage range proof on pre-created proving backend.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_range_proof_check_with_child.html)- range_ - proof_ - check_ - with_ - child
- Check storage range proof with child trie included, generated by
`prove_range_read_with_child_with_size`call.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_range_proof_check_with_child_on_proving_backend.html)- range_ - proof_ - check_ - with_ - child_ - on_ - proving_ - backend
- Check storage range proof on pre-created proving backend.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Child](https://docs.rs/type.ChildStorageCollection.html)- Storage - Collection
- In memory arrays of storage values for multiple child tries.
- [DBValue](https://docs.rs/type.DBValue.html)
- Database value
- [Default](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultError.html)- Error
- Default error type to use with state machine trie backend.
- [Default](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultHandler.html)- Handler
- Default handler of the execution manager.
- [InMemory](https://docs.rs/type.InMemoryBackend.html)- Backend
- Trie backend with in-memory storage.
- [MemoryDB](https://docs.rs/type.MemoryDB.html)
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait. This uses a noops`KeyFunction`(key addressing must be hashed or using an encoding scheme that avoid key conflict).
- [Offchain](https://docs.rs/type.OffchainChangesCollection.html)- Changes - Collection
- In memory array of storage values.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/type.StorageCollection.html)- Collection
- In memory array of storage values.

- Storage key.

- Storage value.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutV0.html)- MutV0
- Persistent trie database write-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutV1.html)- MutV1
- Persistent trie database write-access interface for a given hasher.

A struct containing arguments for iterating over the storage.

## Fields (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

## This struct is marked as non-exhaustive

`Struct { .. }` syntax; cannot be matched against without a wildcard `..`; and struct update syntax will not work.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.prefix)

`prefix: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'a [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]>The prefix of the keys over which to iterate.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.start_at)

`start_at: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'a [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]>The prefix from which to start the iteration from.

This is inclusive and the iteration will include the key which is specified here.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.start_at_exclusive)

`start_at_exclusive: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)If this is `true` then the iteration will *not* include
the key specified in `start_at`, if there is such a key.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.child_info)

`child_info: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ChildInfo](https://docs.rs/sp-storage/25.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_storage/enum.ChildInfo.html)>The info of the child trie over which to iterate over.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.stop_on_incomplete_database)

`stop_on_incomplete_database: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether to stop iteration when a missing trie node is reached.

When a missing trie node is reached the iterator will:

- return an error if this is set to `false`(default)
- return `None`if this is set to`true`

# sp_state_machine::backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/sp_state_machine/backend/index.html

## Expand description

State machine backends. These manage the code and storage of contracts.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/struct.BackendRuntimeCode.html)- Runtime - Code
- Wrapper to create a `RuntimeCode``Backend`
- [Iter](https://docs.rs/struct.IterArgs.html)- Args
- A struct containing arguments for iterating over the storage.
- [Keys](https://docs.rs/struct.KeysIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator over storage keys.
- [Pairs](https://docs.rs/struct.PairsIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator over storage keys and values.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [TryPending](https://docs.rs/enum.TryPendingCode.html)- Code
- Whether to to take `:pending_code`into account when fetching the runtime code.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AsTrie](https://docs.rs/trait.AsTrieBackend.html)- Backend
- Something that can be converted into a `TrieBackend`
- [Backend](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html)
- A state backend is used to read state data and can have changes committed to it.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/trait.StorageIterator.html)- Iterator
- A trait for a raw storage iterator.

# debug in sp_state_machine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/sp_state_machine/macro.debug.html

```
macro_rules! debug {
    (logger: $logger:expr, target: $target:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    (logger: $logger:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    ($($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Logs a message at the debug level.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use log::debug;
let pos = Position { x: 3.234, y: -1.223 };
debug!("New position: x: {}, y: {}", pos.x, pos.y);
debug!(target: "app_events", "New position: x: {}, y: {}", pos.x, pos.y);
debug!(logger: my_logger, "New position: x: {}, y: {}", pos.x, pos.y);
```

---

# log_error in sp_state_machine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/sp_state_machine/macro.log_error.html

```
macro_rules! log_error {
    (logger: $logger:expr, target: $target:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    (logger: $logger:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    ($($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Logs a message at the error level.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use log::error;
let (err_info, port) = ("No connection", 22);
error!("Error: {err_info} on port {port}");
error!(target: "app_events", "App Error: {err_info}, Port: {port}");
error!(logger: my_logger, "App Error: {err_info}, Port: {port}");
```

    (name: $name:expr, $($k:ident).+ $($field:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (name: $name:expr, ?$($k:ident).+ $($field:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (name: $name:expr, %$($k:ident).+ $($field:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (name: $name:expr, $($arg:tt)+ ) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, { $($field:tt)* }, $($arg:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, $($k:ident).+ $($field:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, ?$($k:ident).+ $($field:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, %$($k:ident).+ $($field:tt)* ) => { ... };
    (target: $target:expr, $($arg:tt)+ ) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, { $($field:tt)+ }, $($arg:tt)+ ) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, $($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, ?$($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, %$($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, $($k:ident).+, $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, ?$($k:ident).+, $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, %$($k:ident).+, $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (parent: $parent:expr, $($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
    ({ $($field:tt)+ }, $($arg:tt)+ ) => { ... };
    ($($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (?$($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (%$($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($($k:ident).+, $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (?$($k:ident).+, $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (%$($k:ident).+, $($field:tt)*) => { ... };
    (?$($k:ident).+) => { ... };
    (%$($k:ident).+) => { ... };
    ($($k:ident).+) => { ... };
    ($($arg:tt)+) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Constructs an event at the trace level.

This functions similarly to the [ event!](https://docs.rs/tracing/0.1.44/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing/macro.event.html) macro. See

[the top-level documentation](https://docs.rs/tracing/0.1.44/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing/index.html#using-the-macros)for details on the syntax accepted by this macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use tracing::trace;
let pos = Position { x: 3.234, y: -1.223 };
let origin_dist = pos.dist(Position::ORIGIN);
trace!(position = ?pos, ?origin_dist);
trace!(
    target: "app_events",
    position = ?pos,
    "x is {} and y is {}",
    if pos.x >= 0.0 { "positive" } else { "negative" },
    if pos.y >= 0.0 { "positive" } else { "negative" }
);
trace!(name: "completed", position = ?pos);
```

pub struct Ext<'a, H, B>{
    pub id:
```
[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html),
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

Wraps a read-only backend, call executor, and current overlayed changes.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.id)

`id: `[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)Pseudo-unique id used for tracing.

It allows changes to be modified using nestable transactions.

    prefix: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
) -> [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)

Removes all key-value pairs which keys share the given prefix.

Can be rolled back or committed when called inside a transaction

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#422-426)#### pub fn [transaction_depth](https://docs.rs#method.transaction_depth)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#422-426)

#### pub fn [transaction_depth](https://docs.rs#method.transaction_depth)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Returns the current nesting depth of the transaction stack.

A value of zero means that no transaction is open and changes are committed on write.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#435-441)#### pub fn [start_transaction](https://docs.rs#method.start_transaction)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#435-441)

#### pub fn [start_transaction](https://docs.rs#method.start_transaction)(&mut self)

Start a new nested transaction.

This allows to either commit or roll back all changes that where made while this
transaction was open. Any transaction must be closed by either `rollback_transaction` or
`commit_transaction` before this overlay can be converted into storage changes.

Changes made without any open transaction are committed immediately.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#447-462)#### pub fn [rollback_transaction](https://docs.rs#method.rollback_transaction)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), NoOpenTransaction>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#447-462)

#### pub fn [rollback_transaction](https://docs.rs#method.rollback_transaction)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), NoOpenTransaction>

Rollback the last transaction started by `start_transaction`.

Any changes made during that transaction are discarded. Returns an error if there is no open transaction that can be rolled back.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#468-480)#### pub fn [commit_transaction](https://docs.rs#method.commit_transaction)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), NoOpenTransaction>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#468-480)

#### pub fn [commit_transaction](https://docs.rs#method.commit_transaction)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), NoOpenTransaction>

Commit the last transaction started by `start_transaction`.

Any changes made during that transaction are committed. Returns an error if there is no open transaction that can be committed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#486-498)#### pub fn [enter_runtime](https://docs.rs#method.enter_runtime)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), AlreadyInRuntime>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#486-498)

#### pub fn [enter_runtime](https://docs.rs#method.enter_runtime)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), AlreadyInRuntime>

Call this before transferring control to the runtime.

This protects all existing transactions from being removed by the runtime. Calling this while already inside the runtime will return an error.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#504-516)#### pub fn [exit_runtime](https://docs.rs#method.exit_runtime)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), NotInRuntime>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/overlayed_changes/mod.rs.html#504-516)

#### pub fn [exit_runtime](https://docs.rs#method.exit_runtime)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), NotInRuntime>

Call this when control returns from the runtime.

This rollbacks all dangling transaction left open by the runtime. Calling this while outside the runtime will return an error.

# StorageProof in sp_state_machine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/sp_state_machine/struct.StorageProof.html

`pub struct StorageProof { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A proof that some set of key-value pairs are included in the storage trie. The proof contains the storage values so that the partial storage backend can be reconstructed by a verifier that does not already have access to the key-value pairs.

The proof consists of the set of serialized nodes in the storage trie accessed when looking up the keys covered by the proof. Verifying the proof requires constructing the partial trie from the serialized nodes and performing the key lookups.

#### pub fn [empty](https://docs.rs#method.empty)() -> [StorageProof](https://docs.rs/struct.StorageProof.html)

Returns a new empty proof.

An empty proof is capable of only proving trivial statements (ie. that an empty set of key-value pairs exist in storage).

Merges multiple storage proofs covering potentially different sets of keys into one proof covering all keys. The merged proof output may be smaller than the aggregate size of the input proofs due to deduplication of trie nodes.

#### pub fn [from_raw_snapshot](https://docs.rs#method.from_raw_snapshot)(
    raw_storage: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>, ([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>, [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)))>,
    storage_root: H::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out),
    state_version: [StateVersion](https://docs.rs/sp-storage/25.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_storage/enum.StateVersion.html),
) -> Self

Sets raw storage key/values and a root.

This can be used as a fast way to restore the storage state from a backup because the trie does not need to be computed.

Drains the underlying raw storage key/values and returns the root hash.

Useful for backing up the storage in a format that can be quickly re-loaded.

    execute: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)() -> R,
) -> (R, [StorageProof](https://docs.rs/struct.StorageProof.html))

Execute the given closure while `self`, with `proving_backend` as backend, is set as
externalities.

This implementation will wipe the proof recorded in between calls. Consecutive calls will get their own proof from scratch.

Wrap the given [ TrieBackend](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieBackend.html).

This can be used for example if all accesses to the trie should be recorded while some other functionality still uses the non-recording backend.

The backend storage and the cache will be taken from `other`.

# BackendTrustLevel in sp_state_machine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/sp_state_machine/enum.BackendTrustLevel.html

```
pub enum BackendTrustLevel {
    Trusted,
    Untrusted,
}
```
## Expand description

Storage backend trust level.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Trusted)

### Trusted

Panics from trusted backends are considered justified, and never caught.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Untrusted)

### Untrusted

Panics from untrusted backend are caught and interpreted as runtime error. Untrusted backend may be missing some parts of the trie, so panics are not considered fatal.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# ExecutionError in sp_state_machine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-state-machine/0.53.0/sp_state_machine/enum.ExecutionError.html

```
pub enum ExecutionError {
    Backend(
```
[DefaultError](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultError.html)),
    CodeEntryDoesNotExist,
    UnableToGenerateProof,
    InvalidProof,
}## Expand description

Externalities Error.

Externalities are not really allowed to have errors, since it’s assumed that dependent code would not be executed unless externalities were available. This is included for completeness, and as a transition away from the pre-existing framework.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/trie_backend.rs.html#59)#### fn [as_trie_db_cache](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_trie_db_cache)(&self, storage_root: H::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out)) -> Self::[Cache](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieCacheProvider.html#associatedtype.Cache)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_state_machine/trie_backend.rs.html#59)

#### fn [as_trie_db_cache](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_trie_db_cache)(&self, storage_root: H::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out)) -> Self::[Cache](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieCacheProvider.html#associatedtype.Cache)<'_>

Return a [ trie_db::TrieDB](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedb/struct.TrieDB.html) compatible cache.

The `storage_root` parameter *must* be the storage root of the trie this cache is used for.

NOTE: Implementors should use the `storage_root` to differentiate between storage keys that
may belong to different tries.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Value](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedbmut/enum.Value.html)<L>>, [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[TrieError](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/enum.TrieError.html)<<<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Hash](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Hash) as [Hasher](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html)>::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out), <<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Codec](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Codec) as [NodeCodec](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node_codec/trait.NodeCodec.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node_codec/trait.NodeCodec.html#associatedtype.Error)>>>;
    // Provided method
    fn [contains](https://docs.rs#method.contains)(
        &self,
        key: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[TrieError](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/enum.TrieError.html)<<<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Hash](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Hash) as [Hasher](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html)>::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out), <<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Codec](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Codec) as [NodeCodec](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node_codec/trait.NodeCodec.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node_codec/trait.NodeCodec.html#associatedtype.Error)>>> { ... }
}## Expand description

A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#339-341)

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#339-341)

What is the value of the given key in this trie?

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#345-349)

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#345-349)

Insert a `key`/`value` pair into the trie. An empty value is equivalent to removing
`key` from the trie. Returns the old value associated with this key, if it existed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#353)

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#353)

Remove a `key` from the trie. Equivalent to making it equal to the empty
value. Returns the old value associated with this key, if it existed.
